bullets.text: Average written premium per policy lowered across Agency, Direct, and Commercial Auto; personal auto earned premium per car year fell ~4% (Commercial -5%); Progressive believes most significant downward rate adjustments are behind it.
Operating margin down 5.7 pts YOY; net income declined 29%; personal auto CR was 92.5 compared to Q1's 92.9; intentional progression toward a 96 CR is planned and consistent with rate reductions.

Personal Lines surpassed 10M customers; Q2 Personal Lines new applications grew 3% (up 2% for 6M) versus -8% prior year; policy life expectancy improved; Net Promoter Scores showed steady six-month gains.

Written and earned premiums declined YOY; personal auto written premium per unit declined 1%–2% more than earned premium (down ~4%), with earned premium per unit expected to follow written lower in coming months.

Loss trends from reduced frequency were concluded more systemic than cyclical; an unexpected uninsured motorist reserve adjustment in special lines and Commercial Auto is not expected to recur; unfavorable prior-year development affected larger losses.
Direct personal auto PIF +5% YOY, with Internet sales growing fastest; Agency auto PIF fell slightly, though new business growth returned in 32 states; special lines PIF +7%; Commercial Auto PIF +6%.

Advertising spend increased YOY for Q2 and YTD, shifting to TV and Internet while reducing direct mail; media targets the consumer awareness gap regarding service advantages; brand equity measures improved.

Rate changes reflect an explicit trade-off of margin for longer-term customer growth. Progressive is closer to targeted run-rate margins. Management will stay the course following a numerically disappointing quarter.
